editorial_reason: ProofWiki explicitly lists the intersection of all closed supersets (Definition 2) and the least closed containing subset (Definition 3) as equivalent topological closure characterizations. The intersection family is nonempty since the ambient X is closed, including X=empty; both formulations work without T1 or Hausdorff assumptions. Its other descriptions by derived sets and by boundary should not be silently conflated with separate definitions of the derived set, isolated points or boundary. The source's closure = A union boundary form is intentionally excluded from this admission to avoid a premature circular prerequisite when boundary is defined using closure. This context is not algebraic closure, integral closure, or field norm closure.

ProofWiki's closure-minus-interior and intersection-of-closures-of-complements formulas are equivalent for every topological space, with no metric or separation axiom required. The ambient X is part of the object: boundary relative to a subspace can differ from boundary in a larger surrounding space. The page's additional 'closure and exterior' presentation says the boundary consists of points in A not interior or exterior, which fails for points of cl(A)\A and appears mathematically erroneous. Exclude and explicitly flag that formulation from intake instead of copying it or silently endorsing all source definitions. Also avoid using ambiguous overline A for complement: write X\A explicitly.

The direct ProofWiki linear-kernel page presents the zero-preimage definition in general R-modules and separately specializes to vector spaces, where it is also called null space. These are related but have different domain generality, so index as two contextual mathematical meanings grouped under kernel of linear transformation; do not treat arbitrary modules as field vector spaces, or kernels of generic nonadditive mappings as linear kernels. The zero of the CODOMAIN N (or W) is used; the kernel is a subset of the DOMAIN M (or V). Existing independently screened group-homomorphism kernel and categorical universal-property kernel remain distinct broader contexts and must not be overwritten. This page supplies no independent mathematical definition of linear transformation itself.

ProofWiki differentiates a number f′(a) at a single interior point from the derivative function f′:I→R defined pointwise throughout an open interval on which f is differentiable. Its interval-level source explicitly assumes differentiability at every x, so the resulting derivative function has entire domain I; do not silently extend to functions differentiable only on a subset or to one-sided derivatives at endpoints. The preexisting independent OpenStax real derivative-at-an-interior-point source remains untouched; this candidate is a distinct but naturally linked function-valued object. Variable h must approach 0 through nonzero increments lying in the function domain. The notation y′ or d/dx does not create an additional mathematical meaning.
